messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]

Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with shortness of breath, dry coughing and fever, after testing positive for COVID-19. The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation, as he had severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. 
Throughout his 31-day hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The chest X-ray revealed bilateral pneumothoraces, which were confirmed with a chest CT, along with pneumomediastinum. The patient was transferred to a hospital where thoracic surgery was available. Imaging after transfer showed that the pneumothorax had slightly increased without tension physiology. The PEEP was decreased from 8 to 6 cm H20 where it remained till his discharge. On the 31st day of admission the patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation. 

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with COVID-19 and developed severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. Throughout his hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, ARDS, volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure on hospital day 31.

Outcome:
The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure after a prolonged hospital stay.

text:
**U07**

COVID-19 was the condition that caused the admission. Australian (IHACPA/ACCD) guidance sequences U07.1 (COVID-19, virus identified) as the principal diagnosis when COVID-19 is the reason for admission. The ARDS, septic shock and pneumothoraces are then coded as additional diagnoses. I'm recalling that sequencing rule rather than quoting it, so confirm it against the current ICD-10-AM/ACS edition your service uses.
